decisions.text: Ground two squares from a canal becomes 'wetted' by the same technique Stillsand is developing for spilled water on sand. Wetting is not flood water; flood water also wets what it passes. Wetted ground gives plants water; explosive growth uses the wetting up until reapplied, and plants also drink standing flood water above them, lowering it.

asks.text: In your moat and pit-trap scenes the raiders end up as prisoners in the pit. Today that takes one order from the rim: 'capture' on a raider the pit holds, and only if a prisoner bed is down there (built, your 2026-09-17 words: nobody has to go down). A bed cannot be built in a full moat, so as things stand a moat cannot hold prisoners. Which do you picture: (a) they become prisoners by themselves once the pit holds them and the raid gives up, no bed needed; (b) you click 'capture' from the rim as now, but a drained moat counts as a prison without a bed; or (c) as now, bed and click, and the moat sequence uses a pit beside the moat?
asks.decision: Whether being held in a pit makes a raider a prisoner automatically, by one click, or by click plus bed; decides new capture code and whether a moat can be a prison room.
asks.author: rm-role-designer-1793843896

review.why: His words settle that they become prisoners, not how; the choice decides new capture code. Wording narrowed to what the code shows (no bed in a full moat).

asks.text: 'Someone drops in a match from above.' Today a burnable canal lights from any fire on or beside it: a molotov, an incendiary shell, a burning raider (built). There is no order for a colonist to walk to the rim and toss a flame in. Which lights your moat: a new order where a colonist walks to the edge and tosses a flame in (slower, but anyone can do it and you choose the square), or a thrown molotov or a fired incendiary, as now?
asks.decision: Whether a new 'drop a flame' order is built for igniting a liquid from the rim, or vanilla incendiaries are the only lighter.
asks.author: rm-role-designer-1793843896

review.why: True as stated: ignition is any vanilla fire on or beside the liquid; no player drop-a-flame order exists; his words do not say who lights it. 'Torch' replaced: vanilla has no carryable torch.

asks.text: In the pit-trap scene the raiders chop saplings to build a ladder down to their two fallen men. What is built today: raiders who cannot reach you chop a tree, make ladders and climb DOWN, ACROSS and UP a trench to get at you; they do not go down for their own fallen. On screen the two look alike (raiders chopping and carrying wood under your arrows), but in yours they want their men back, and they leave when they cannot. Is the crossing-ladder raid your scene, or must raiders go for their fallen, and give up and run when they cannot?
asks.decision: Whether a new raider 'fetch our fallen from a pit' behaviour is built, or the built trench-crossing ladder is the pit-trap scene's raider half.
asks.author: rm-role-designer-1793843896

review.why: Already answered by his words: the raiders build the ladder 'to retrieve them' and 'are driven off'. Recorded as decision d_raider_fetch_fallen instead.

failure_modes: It works but does not read: the state is right while the screen shows something else (a pit that reads as a labelled trap, a canal that reads as gravel, deep water a pawn just walks out of). In the validated walk only 4 of 43 bars proved anything, so 'passing' can hide this.

The defense spine does not bite in a real raid: the canal is empty or level-broken when the raid comes, the source never visibly pays or refills, fire or slime do not deny the corridor, raiders path round or shelter in the trench. Then 'hold the gate' is not a decision and the mod's reason to exist is gone.

Breadth breaks the colony: pits, hoses, pipes, bridges, thirst, rivers and sprinklers each pass alone but fight together on a long game (hoses under walls, full-list speed down from 346 to ~120 TPS, toggles leaving leftovers, a reload that diverges, a port losing what worked). He experiences it as FlowWorks being broken, whatever any one row says.

root.text: FlowWorks lets you dig into the ground, and the liquids already on the map (water, tar, fuel, slime) flow into what you dug and settle at one level, drawn from a real supply that visibly shrinks and refills slowly. Its main job is deadly earthworks: pits, moats, traps and drawbridges that you fill, drain and set alight at the moment you choose. Ground within two squares of a filled canal is wetted, so plants there have water. The plumbing (pipes, pumps, tanks, hoses, bottles) and reshaping the land use the same liquids and the same supply. The mod is judged first on one raid: raiders swim a deep water moat under a raised drawbridge and tire, a sluice gate drains it, they are held as prisoners in the pit for a while, then chemfuel is pumped in from above and lit.
